world.b: North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported.
world.title: North Korea tests two submarine-launched missiles, state media reports

world.h: Pope Leo's lung recovering well after surgery
world.b: Doctors said a chest X-ray showed good recovery and post-operative tests are normal; the Vatican said Leo has resumed working from the hospital.
world.title: Doctors say Pope Leo's lung has recovered well from surgery and say his post-operative tests normal

world.h: Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 29
world.b: The roof of a private school in Peshawar collapsed Thursday, killing at least 28 children and a teacher and injuring more than 50, officials said.
world.title: School roof collapse kills at least 29, injures more than 3 dozen in Pakistan

world.h: Ukraine strikes Russian refinery as truce ends
world.b: Ukrainian drones set a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region on fire early Thursday, hours after Zelenskyy said a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over.
world.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries, officials say, after brief truce

world.h: Iran war: Missile intercepted near Medina
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a missile around Medina.
world.title: Saudi-led coalition says missile intercepted around Medina

world.h: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of throttling Starlink
world.b: A Zelenskyy adviser said Starlink service was limited overnight for terminals moving over 100mph, curbing Ukraine's ability to fly drones that rely on satellite internet.

world.h: UN warns of food crisis as Hormuz plan stalls
world.b: UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva said Iran and the US must agree within weeks on a plan to move fertiliser through the Strait of Hormuz or parts of Asia and Africa could face a food crisis.

world.h: Israeli strike kills woman in Gaza City
world.b: An Israeli air strike on an apartment block in Gaza City's Al-Rimal neighbourhood killed Reem Asaad Awad, 33, and wounded two others early Wednesday, hospital officials said.

world.h: Russian strikes kill 6 in Ukraine, cut power
world.b: Russian air attacks killed at least six people and left hundreds of thousands without power, days after Trump announced an 'energy ceasefire'.

world.h: Trump: Greenland oil, gas exploration to begin
world.b: Trump said on Truth Social that 'massive' oil, gas and mineral exploration is set to begin in Greenland, a self-governing Danish territory.

world.h: UN sees 'window' for peace in eastern DR Congo
world.b: UN Great Lakes envoy Huang Xia told the Security Council that US- and Qatar-led peace processes have made 'notable progress' in eastern DR Congo.

national.h: Some cut from ACA rolls are being added back
national.b: After the administration dropped 760,000 people from Affordable Care Act plans citing fraud, CMS has reinstated a small number whose coverage should not have been canceled, KFF Health News reports.
national.title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back

national.h: Abbott keeps Texas border emergency going
national.b: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has renewed or amended his border disaster proclamation at least 69 times, 21 under Trump, even as the administration reports historic lows in crossings.
national.title: Trump Says the Border Is Secure. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott Keeps Declaring an Emergency.

national.h: OpenAI bugging suspect booked one-way flight
national.b: Prosecutors say former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, accused of bugging the company's headquarters, had booked a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia before his arrest.
national.title: OpenAI bugging suspect allegedly booked one-way trip to Saudi Arabia

national.h: ICE rejects call for auto-recording body cameras
national.b: ICE rejected a Government Accountability Office report recommending its agents wear body cameras that activate automatically.

national.h: Iowa water quality, cancer rates now campaign issue
national.b: Nitrate pollution from farm runoff, long a taboo topic in Iowa politics, is now the focus of debates and ads from candidates of both parties.
ProPublica reports that women who said they were victims, not abusers, were held for months at an immigration detention center in west Michigan as protections for abuse victims eroded.
national.title: These Women Were Trying to Escape Domestic Abuse. ICE Detained Them Instead.

national.h: Data centers clash with NM, El Paso climate plans
national.b: Data center projects in New Mexico and El Paso are moving forward even though both places recently adopted plans to sharply cut greenhouse gas emissions, ProPublica reports.
national.title: New Mexico and El Paso Spent Millions on Climate Plans. Three New Data Centers Could Undo Them.

politics.h: Missouri GOP targets how top judges are picked
politics.b: After court losses, Missouri Republicans want to change the merit-based Missouri Plan that has chosen the state's top judges since the 1940s, ProPublica reports.
politics.title: Frustrated by Losses in the Courts, Missouri Republicans Want to Change How Top Judges Are Selected

politics.h: Administration seeks to strip Omar's citizenship
politics.b: The Trump administration is investigating Rep. Ilhan Omar to revoke her citizenship and eventually deport her, the Wall Street Journal reported, with grand jury subpoenas issued to relatives.
politics.title: Trump administration seeks to strip Ilhan Omar of US citizenship: WSJ

politics.b: At a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, Trump said people who leak government information to the media should be shot.
politics.title: Trump suggests those who leak government information should ‘be shot’

politics.h: Lisa Cook's lawyers call White House hearing biased
politics.b: Fed Governor Lisa Cook won't attend a Nov. 5 hearing before a White House panel; her lawyer said the earliest she could appear is after the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.
politics.title: Lawyers for Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook say White House hearing set up by Trump is 'biased'

politics.h: GOP super PAC pulls out of four House races
politics.b: The Congressional Leadership Fund canceled spending in four races and boosted 16 others, while Democrats eye openings in Republican-held districts.

international.h: Teen dies as heavy rain floods Istanbul
international.b: A 14-year-old boy was electrocuted after stepping into a puddle in Istanbul's Fatih district as heavy rain caved in roads and snarled traffic.
international.title: Teenager dies as heavy rain floods Istanbul

international.b: The Palestinian Prisoner's Society says Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since October 2023, with at least 350 now in Israeli prisons.
international.title: Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since 2023: report

international.b: President Laura Fernandez opened a high-security prison for organised crime amid near-record homicides, as Bukele-style crackdowns spread across Latin America.

international.h: Mexico orders platforms to shield minors
international.b: President Claudia Sheinbaum signed a decree requiring TikTok, Meta, X and others to restrict violent and sexual content for children and remove risky material from minors' profiles.

international.h: Ex-Shin Bet chief sues Netanyahu for defamation
international.b: Ronen Bar accused Netanyahu of lying to cover himself over the October 7 attack, filing suit ahead of Israel's October 27 election.
A 39-year-old man, a close relative of Kenya's first Ebola patient, fell ill while already in quarantine, the Health Ministry said.

international.h: Colombia opens embassy to Israel in Jerusalem
international.b: Colombia inaugurated an embassy in Jerusalem, joining a small group of countries backing Israel's claim to the city; Palestinian officials denounced the move.

international.h: Iraq PM vows no attacks on Saudis from Iraq
international.b: On his first visit to Riyadh since taking office in May, Iraqi PM Ali Faleh al-Zaidi assured Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that Iraqi territory will not be used to launch attacks on Saudi Arabia.

international.h: Settlers set fire to West Bank mosque
international.b: Israeli settlers set fire to a mosque, an olive tree and a vehicle while raiding the village of Mikhmas early Wednesday, Wafa reported, as Israeli forces raided villages across the territory.

international.h: Namibia meat markets hit by cattle disease
international.b: A cattle disease outbreak has emptied stalls at Windhoek's largest meat market as the EU suspends several Namibian meat imports.

international.h: China, North Korea to open Yalu River bridge
international.b: The New Yalu River Bridge opens to traffic Thursday, Xinhua reports. China finished its side in 2014, but North Korea left its side unfinished for years.

international.h: West Bank Palestinians have no say in Israel vote
international.b: Nearly three million Palestinians in the occupied West Bank cannot vote in Israel's Oct. 27 election, unlike 700,000 Jewish settlers living there.

international.h: Nord Stream sabotage trial opens in Germany
international.b: A Ukrainian former military officer went on trial in Hamburg, accused of organising the 2022 blasts on the Nord Stream gas pipelines. The trial is expected to run into February.

international.h: Israel returns 22 stolen artefacts to Greece
international.b: Israel returned 22 ancient artefacts stolen from Greece. Officials gave no details on how they were found.

international.h: Jamaica takes first third-country US deportees
international.b: Twenty-two deportees from the US arrived in Kingston on Tuesday, Jamaica's first third-country deportations under expanding Trump administration agreements.
Colombia's transitional justice tribunal charged 10 former FARC members with war crimes and crimes against humanity against Indigenous people between 1996 and 2016.

international.h: Israeli strike kills one in Gaza City
international.b: An Israeli air strike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tuffah neighbourhood killed one person, and journalists were wounded in the occupied West Bank.

international.h: Fire hits Albania Education Ministry in protests
international.b: Protesters broke into Albania's Education Ministry in Tirana overnight and lit a fire, police said, with 16 arrests, as student protests demanding PM Edi Rama's resignation entered a third day.

business.h: Virginia's Data Center Alley may be hitting a limit
business.b: Loudoun County, home to the world's highest concentration of data centers, faces questions about what happens if growth slows.
business.title: "Data Center Alley" in suburban Virginia may be hitting a dead end

business.h: IMF chief urges wealthy nations to cut debt
business.b: Kristalina Georgieva said growth alone cannot fix US debt of more than $40 trillion, speaking at the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, with a 0.6% monthly jump, the biggest in five months, as the Iran war keeps gas prices high.

business.h: Singapore economy grows 5.4% on AI boom
business.b: Singapore's GDP grew 5.4% year-on-year in the third quarter, down from 6.2% in the second, advance estimates showed.

business.h: Bank of America fined $1.2B by Treasury
business.b: The US Treasury imposed more than $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America for anti-money laundering and sanctions violations.

sports.b: Milwaukee rallied after Blake Snell was left in for the seventh inning, pushing the Dodgers to the brink of elimination.
sports.title: Dodgers manager Dave Roberts explains leaving Blake Snell in before costly back-to-back home runs in Game 3

sports.h: Real Madrid edges Roma 4-3 in Mourinho return
sports.b: Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid rallied for a late 4-3 Champions League win at Roma, while PSG routed Manchester City.
sports.title: UEFA Champions League scores, schedule: Manchester City vs. PSG highlights Matchday 2

sports.h: ALCS Game 3 moved to 1 p.m. for rain
sports.b: MLB moved Thursday's Rays-Guardians Game 3 in Cleveland up from 6 p.m. to 1 p.m. ET because of forecast rain; the series is tied 1-1.

sports.h: Rams cut kicker Mevis after loss to Bills
sports.b: The Rams are releasing Harrison Mevis, who missed two field goals including a 48-yard overtime try, and signing Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad.

sports.h: Dream, Valkyries set for WNBA Finals
sports.b: Atlanta and Golden State, neither of which has won a WNBA title, meet in the Finals starting Oct. 17. The Dream are 5-0 in the playoffs.
sports.title: 2026 WNBA playoffs bracket: WNBA Finals schedule tweaked so Dream can use larger venue

sports.b: CBS Sports' annual ranking of the NBA's top 100 players puts Victor Wembanyama at No. 1 entering the 2026-27 season.

sports.h: Bills beat Rams 37-34 in OT; punch thrown after
sports.b: Buffalo beat the Rams 37-34 in overtime Monday night. Afterward, Rams lineman Alaric Jackson threw an apparent punch at Bills pass-rusher Bradley Chubb.

local.h: Comptroller backs off pension investment in Israel bonds
local.b: NYC Comptroller Mark Levine said he won't invest city pension funds in Israel bonds.
local.title: Early Addition: NYC comptroller backs off investing city pension funds in Israel bonds

local.h: Police investigate death of 5-year-old in Queens
local.b: Police found the girl unconscious after an apparent assault at a Richmond Hill home Wednesday evening, after her mother called 911.
local.title: NYPD investigating after 5-year-old Queens girl found dead

local.h: Man shot by ICE says agents never identified selves
local.b: The man wounded by immigration agents in Marble Hill last week says he did not know they were ICE until he woke up in the hospital.
local.title: Man shot by ICE in NYC's Marble Hill said federal officers never identified themselves

local.h: National Grid gas bills to rise this winter
local.b: About 1.2 million customers in Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island will pay an average $87 more over five winter months.
local.title: National Grid customers in NYC will see higher gas bills this winter

local.h: Suspects in detective stabbing plead not guilty
local.b: Sneider Mejia, 24, and D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, pleaded not guilty to charges including attempted murder of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx.
local.title: 2 men accused of stabbing off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx plead not guilty

local.h: Gas leaks cost New Yorkers $300M a year
local.b: Nearly 2% of the natural gas city customers pay for escapes into the air, Columbia University researchers found.
local.title: New Yorkers are paying $300 million for natural gas they don't even use

local.h: Hit-and-run suspect caught fleeing to Uzbekistan
local.b: Police arrested Sobirjon Abdurazakov, 22, at the airport as he tried to leave the country after a deadly Brooklyn crash, the NYPD says.
local.title: Hit-and-run driver arrested trying to flee to Uzbekistan after deadly crash, NYPD says

local.h: Measles outbreak bigger than state count
local.b: Health officials in Otsego and Seneca counties say many more measles cases are going unreported than the state dashboard shows.
local.title: NY measles outbreak more widespread than official count, health officials say

local.h: Bronx casino to anchor Ferry Point Park makeover
local.b: Bally's Bronx will sit in the middle of a $160 million Ferry Point Park makeover with new playgrounds and athletic fields; the community board weighs in Thursday.
local.title: The Bronx is getting a new casino and a reimagined Ferry Point Park, too
